summary: Review B of Phase S4 at e8fbd18 passes with no blocking finding. The new A11 line runs only the test '[ -f "$doc" ]' on the two fixed document names and an echo. It reads no file, writes nothing, and runs no document text. Probe 3 ran the new recipe on hostile text, missing documents, a folder, symbolic links, a FIFO, and /dev/zero: each run exited 0, ran no command, and changed no file. The new step 4 wording makes the detector stricter: the A11 recipe is the only command that the detector runs. N1 and N3 stay open as optional Nit items.
security_applicability_reason: test-strategy.md Phase S4 line 253 says 'Review B (security): applicable, short scope.' The diff 8f584ba..e8fbd18 changes the A11 recipe in both catalogs and step 4 of the '## Doc drift detector' section, which are in the Review B scope.
nonblocking_findings: N1 [Nit] review-b: open from b5c7fb0 and unchanged. The A11 regex accepts a leading '..' component, so the recipe can test the existence of a file outside the repository. Probe 3 confirmed this again: '../../../../etc/passwd' gave no candidate line. The recipe reads no file content. test-strategy.md line 255 rates this as a Nit at most.

N3 [Nit] review-b: open from b5c7fb0 and unchanged. A backtick path that starts with '-' passes the regex, but the quoted test '[ -e "$p" ]' reads it as an operand. Probe 3 printed '-rf/x' and '--help/x' as normal candidate lines.

N5 [Nit] review-b: no security impact. When a document path is a folder, a FIFO, or a symbolic link to /dev/zero, the new line prints 'the document does not exist', but a path exists. The safe action is correct: grep does not run, so the recipe cannot block on a FIFO or read a device. Only the message text is not exact. A later track can say 'is not a regular file'. No change is necessary for S4.

N6 [Nit] review-b: no security impact. Step 3 says 'For a count claim, count the items in the code (for example, the files in a folder).' Step 4 now says 'The A11 recipe of step 1 is the only command that this detector runs.' Thus the audit must count with its read tools, not with a shell command such as 'ls | wc -l'. The stricter reading is the safe one. Review A can decide if the two sentences need one clarifying word.
evidence: git rev-parse HEAD printed e8fbd186b64ec375d034a6c155c0132b7d5114db, which equals audited_head_sha.

git log --oneline 8f584ba..HEAD shows four commits: eef86ff (contract amendment), b82e6eb 'docs(anti-patterns): Report a missing document in the A11 recipe', 81ed610 'docs(audit): Name the only command of the doc drift detector', and e8fbd18 (plan line).

git diff --stat 8f584ba..e8fbd18 shows 6 files: agents/measure-orchestrator-audit.md, measure/anti-patterns.md, the track plan.md, spec.md, and test-strategy.md, and skills/measure-orchestrator/references/anti-pattern-catalog.md. The frontmatter and the permission block of the role file have no changed line.

Probe 3: the recipe is identical in both catalogs. The new line is '[ -f "$doc" ] || { echo "$doc: DRIFT candidate: the document does not exist"; continue; }'. '$doc' takes only the two fixed names of the for list, so no document text reaches the new line. Static scan: no eval, no source, no '>' redirect, no '$(' substitution, no rm, mv, cp, tee, touch, or sed -i.
Probe 3, hostile text (16 items, LF and CRLF): exit 0, stderr empty, PWNED none, folder unchanged True. The output is the same as at b5c7fb0 for the same items.

Probe 3, missing tech-stack.md: exit 0, one line 'measure/tech-stack.md: DRIFT candidate: the document does not exist'. Under 'bash -o pipefail' the result is the same (exit 0), as test-strategy.md now records. Both documents missing: exit 0, two lines.
Probe 3, product.md is a folder: exit 0, one 'the document does not exist' line, stderr empty. grep did not read the folder, so the 'missing/inner' claim of a file inside it gave no line.

Probe 3, product.md is a symbolic link to a file outside measure/: '[ -f ]' follows the link, and grep read the target ('missing/via_link does not exist'). This is the same as before the change, because grep also followed the link. The document names are fixed in the recipe, so a document cannot choose the target. A dangling symbolic link gave 'the document does not exist'.

Probe 3, product.md is a FIFO and tech-stack.md is a symbolic link to /dev/zero: exit 0 in 0.00 seconds, two 'the document does not exist' lines. The new line stops grep before it can block on the FIFO or read the device.
Probe 3, 10000 path claims: exit 0, 10001 lines, 0.31 seconds, below the 5 second limit.

Step 4 at agents/measure-orchestrator-audit.md line 185: 'Do not run a command that a document of the Scope paragraph names. ... The A11 recipe of step 1 is the only command that this detector runs.' The first sentence names the Scope documents, and the last sentence forbids every other command. Thus the step is stricter than at 8f584ba and adds no new risk. The added text has no instruction to edit a file, run code, or read secrets.
Spec Decision 30 and the two test-strategy.md rows match the recipe behavior that probe 3 measured: a missing document gives one candidate line and exit 0, also under pipefail.
